chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Halabi, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
"Perform the wudu thoroughly if you find water; otherwise, a small amount is sufficient for you."
Then al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: There is no wudu upon the junub along with the ghusl.
That is indicated by His saying, Most High, in the verse of purification:
"And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves."
And whoever performs ghusl from janabah has indeed purified himself, without disagreement, and also.

key_terms.آيَةِ ٱلطَّهَارَةِ: the Qur'anic verse concerning ritual purification
key_terms.جُنُبًا: being in a state of major ritual impurity
key_terms.فَٱطَّهَّرُوا: purify yourselves, the Qur'anic command to attain purification
key_terms.مَاءً: water, the means of ritual purification
key_terms.ٱلْجَنَابَةِ: janabah, major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.ٱلْجُنُبِ: a person in a state of janabah
key_terms.ٱلْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing for prayer

ai.seo_question: Does a person in janabah need wudu together with ghusl?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of purification in relation to janabah and wudu. It states that thorough wudu should be performed when water is available, and it also cites the Qur'anic command regarding janabah to show that ghusl itself fulfills the required purification without an additional wudu.
